small_guidance:
- The kernel recomputes the full conv for every output position then reduces over OC; try a larger BLOCK_M (e.g. 128) with BLOCK_N=64 so a single program covers more output spatial elements while iterating all OC tiles, amortizing the x_vals loads across more rows.
- Add autotune configs with BLOCK_N equal to OC (128) so `num_oc_tiles=1` and the outer OC loop is eliminated; combinations like (BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=2) and (BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32, num_warps=8, num_stages=2) are worth trying — verify each fits the ~132 KB SMEM budget.
- Precompute kh/kw/ic decomposition outside the k-loop only once per program by ordering K as (KH,KW,IC) with IC innermost so `ic = k % IC` and only KH·KW unique (kh,kw) — current layout already does this; consider hoisting `ih*(W*IC)+iw*IC` so the inner-loop offset math is just `+ ic`.
large_guidance:
- Switch to an implicit-GEMM where each program owns one (N, output-tile of BLOCK_M pixels) and ALL OC channels at once (BLOCK_N = OC = 128). The accumulator is BLOCK_M×OC in registers; after the K-loop, fuse bias + scale + channel-wise min in registers and write only BLOCK_M scalars. This eliminates the outer oc_tile loop and the redundant reloading of x for each OC tile (currently x is reloaded `OC/BLOCK_N` times).
- Keep weight in (KH, KW, IC, OC) NHWC layout (already done) and stage the K reduction as an outer loop over (kh,kw) with an inner loop over IC in BLOCK_K chunks; this makes the x-gather index math `ih*(W*IC)+iw*IC+ic` with constant (kh,kw) per outer iter and lets `tl.dot` see a clean [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K] × [BLOCK_K, OC] GEMM.
- Consider a persistent / split-K-free design where one program handles a (N, output row) — with W=254 output cols, BLOCK_M=256 covers a full row; this gives perfect coalescing for the final min store and keeps the working set on-chip.
